title: Finalizers, SafeHandle and the dispose pattern
body: A finalizer (`~Resource() { ... }`) runs on a GC thread some time after an object becomes unreachable, if ever before process exit. It is a last-chance safety net for unmanaged resources when callers forget to dispose, not a substitute for `Dispose`. Finalizable objects survive at least one extra collection and slow the GC, so most classes should not have one.

Instead of writing finalizers, wrap native handles in a `SafeHandle` subclass (such as `SafeFileHandle`). SafeHandle has a reliable finalizer, protects against handle recycling races and makes your class's `Dispose` simply call `handle.Dispose()`. Classes that only hold managed disposables never need a finalizer.

The full dispose pattern for unsealed classes uses `protected virtual void Dispose(bool disposing)`. `Dispose()` calls `Dispose(true)` and then `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)`; a finalizer, if present, calls `Dispose(false)`. When `disposing` is false you must not touch other managed objects, because they may already have been finalized. Derived classes override `Dispose(bool)` and call `base.Dispose(disposing)`.

`GC.SuppressFinalize(this)` tells the runtime the finalizer no longer needs to run, removing the extra cost once cleanup has happened deterministically. Seal classes when you can; a sealed class can use a simple `Dispose()` without the virtual pattern.
Check whether a type truly owns an unmanaged resource. If not, do not add a finalizer; if so, prefer SafeHandle, and make sure finalizer code touches only that resource.

challenge: Write a sealed class Pinned holding a GCHandle that pins a byte[] in its constructor and frees it in Dispose, with a finalizer fallback (the GC never frees a pinned handle, so a forgotten Dispose would leak the array) and GC.SuppressFinalize in Dispose. Print IsAllocated before and after a using block.

question: Why should a finalizer not use other managed objects referenced by fields?
correct: They may already have been finalized or collected in the same cycle
wrong: Managed objects are always null during finalization
reasoning: Finalization order is undefined; only touch the unmanaged resource the object owns. Prefer SafeHandle.
